summary: Acitretin is a systemic retinoid for severe psoriasis in adults, prescribed only by clinicians experienced with systemic retinoids. It carries a boxed warning for severe teratogenicity: it must never be used in pregnancy, and because concurrent alcohol can convert acitretin to long-lived etretinate, females of childbearing potential must avoid pregnancy and alcohol during therapy and for 3 years (pregnancy) / 2 months (alcohol) afterward, with no blood donation for 3 years. Other key risks are hepatotoxicity, marked hyperlipidemia, hypervitaminosis-A mucocutaneous effects, pseudotumor cerebri (especially with tetracyclines), and skeletal changes.
indications: Treatment of severe psoriasis in adults

dosage.d: 25-50 mg once daily, given as a single dose with the main meal
dosage.n: Individualize; many side effects are dose-related
Adjust to response and tolerability; relapse common after stopping
Decrease UV dose because of additive photosensitivity

admin: Take as a single daily dose with the main meal for optimal absorption
Must be prescribed only by clinicians experienced in systemic retinoid use
For females of reproductive potential: confirm two negative pregnancy tests before starting, begin on day 2 or 3 of a normal menstrual period, and use two effective forms of contraception
Dispense no more than a one-month supply and give the Medication Guide each time
No blood donation during therapy and for 3 years afterward (to avoid transfusing a pregnant recipient)
moa: The exact mechanism is unknown. Acitretin is the active metabolite of etretinate and, like other retinoids, modulates epidermal cell proliferation and differentiation and exerts anti-inflammatory effects through nuclear retinoic-acid receptors, normalizing the hyperproliferative, abnormally differentiated keratinocytes of psoriasis.

absolute: Pregnancy or intent to become pregnant during therapy or within 3 years after (Pregnancy Category X)
Females unable to use reliable contraception
Hypersensitivity to acitretin, other retinoids or excipients
relative: Concomitant use of other hepatotoxic or photosensitizing drugs
monitor: Pregnancy tests (before, monthly during, and after)

preg: ABSOLUTELY CONTRAINDICATED (Pregnancy Category X). Acitretin causes severe major human fetal abnormalities (CNS, craniofacial, skeletal, cardiovascular and limb defects). Females must not be pregnant at initiation, must not become pregnant during therapy, and must avoid pregnancy for at least 3 YEARS after stopping, because alcohol-driven conversion to etretinate (very long half-life, stored in fat) prolongs teratogenic risk. Two effective contraceptive methods are required.
lact: Contraindicated. Etretinate is excreted in animal milk and acitretin has been reported in human milk; nursing mothers must not receive acitretin because of the potential for serious adverse effects in the infant.
renal: Contraindicated in severely impaired renal function.
hepatic: Contraindicated in severely impaired liver function. Acitretin is hepatotoxic - obtain LFTs before therapy, every 1-2 weeks until stable, then periodically; discontinue if hepatotoxicity develops. Do not combine with methotrexate.

major: Ethanol (in females of childbearing potential) - promotes conversion of acitretin to long-acting teratogenic etretinate; strictly prohibited during and for 2 months after therapy
Methotrexate - increased risk of hepatitis; combination contraindicated
Tetracyclines - additive raised intracranial pressure (pseudotumor cerebri); contraindicated
Vitamin A / other retinoids - additive hypervitaminosis A toxicity
Progestin-only ('mini-pill') contraceptives - may be inadequate; use two reliable methods
moderate: Phenytoin - acitretin may displace protein binding
Phototherapy/UV and photosensitizing drugs - additive photosensitivity
minor: No significant interaction observed with cimetidine, digoxin
interactions.food: Take with the main meal; food substantially increases absorption.
interactions.alcohol: Females of childbearing potential MUST NOT drink alcohol during treatment and for 2 months after, because ethanol promotes formation of long-lived teratogenic etretinate.
interactions.diagnostics: Frequently raises triglycerides, cholesterol and liver transaminases; lowers HDL; may impair glucose control; can cause skeletal hyperostosis on imaging.

emergency: Severe headache with visual changes/vomiting (pseudotumor cerebri)
Signs of liver failure (jaundice, dark urine)

monitoring: Pregnancy tests in females of reproductive potential - before, monthly during, and after therapy
Liver function tests before, every 1-2 weeks until stable, then periodically
Visual symptoms and signs of raised intracranial pressure
counsel: This drug causes severe birth defects - you must not be pregnant and must use two reliable contraceptive methods, avoiding pregnancy for 3 years after stopping
Do NOT drink any alcohol during treatment and for 2 months afterward if you can become pregnant
Do not donate blood during therapy or for 3 years after
Dry lips, skin, eyes and some hair thinning are expected; use lip balm and moisturizers
Report severe headaches with vision changes, yellowing of the skin/eyes, severe stomach pain, mood changes or suicidal thoughts; avoid vitamin A supplements and tell your doctor about all medicines
pk: Skin improvement over weeks; steady state in ~3 weeks
Plasma peak ~2-5 hours (mean ~2.7 h) after a dose with food
~49 h (acitretin); ~63 h (cis-acitretin); etretinate metabolite can persist ~120 days
Once-daily dosing; relapse usual after discontinuation
Store at 20-25 C; protect from light; avoid heat and humidity once opened
pearls: Boxed warning - profound teratogen; pregnancy contraindicated and must be avoided for 3 YEARS after stopping
Alcohol converts acitretin to etretinate (very long half-life) - ban alcohol in women of childbearing potential during and 2 months after
No blood donation during therapy and for 3 years afterward
Contraindicated with methotrexate (hepatitis) and tetracyclines (pseudotumor cerebri)
Hepatotoxic and markedly raises triglycerides - monitor LFTs and fasting lipids closely
missed: If a dose is missed, take it with food as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose - do not take two doses together. Never increase the dose to make up.
overdose: Overdose produces acute hypervitaminosis-A effects (headache, vertigo). Withdraw acitretin at once and give supportive care; acute toxicity is generally low. Any female of childbearing potential who overdoses must have a pregnancy test and be counseled about birth-defect risk and the 3-year contraception requirement.
